diagnosis: Astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 4, IDH-mutant.
Minimally invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC), 35 mm, arising in the right thyroid lobe; subsequent iodine-avid pulmonary metastases detected on post-ablation imaging.
Stage IB breast carcinoma, pT1b pN0 M0. Triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast.
Hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of cirrhosis with symptomatic portal decompensation.
High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, stage IV at diagnosis on 25 December 2019; recurrent/progressive disease with last documented progression/relapse on 24 September 2025.
Metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid) with hepatic metastases, mesenteric involvement, and later extensive osseous metastases.

Widely invasive/angioinvasive oncocytic (Hürthle cell) follicular thyroid carcinoma, initially misclassified as follicular adenoma on original pathology, with recurrent subcutaneous soft-tissue metastatic deposits in the neck/chest inlet region. Subsequent 2021 recurrent deposit showed progression to poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma, oncocytic type, by Memorial criteria.
Olfactory neuroblastoma (esthesioneuroblastoma), locally advanced at presentation, with no regional nodal or distant metastatic disease on initial staging workup.

Malignant melanoma involving a left supraclavicular cervical lymph node, presenting as nodal melanoma with no identifiable primary lesion on clinical examination. History included basal cell carcinoma of the cheek and melanoma in situ of the posterior neck in 1999.

Cervical squamous cell carcinoma diagnosed in 2015. Clinical examination showed a bleeding exophytic cervical lesion with superinfection and cervical induration, without clinical vaginal or parametrial involvement. Initial body CT showed no metastatic disease. Surgical pathology demonstrated nodal involvement in 1 of 19 lymph nodes examined, involving a left iliac node. The case was documented as surgical stage IIIB.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with extensive cervical nodal metastases and bilateral pulmonary metastases.
Left hilar mass; cancer diagnosis.
Solid-cystic sellar/suprasellar craniopharyngioma, WHO grade 1, with postoperative residual suprasellar disease.
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma involving the left base of tongue with metastatic left cervical nodal disease.
Skull base extra-axial cystic lesion centered in the pre-/suprasellar region, radiologically favored to represent an epidermoid cyst.
Prostatic adenocarcinoma, Gleason score 3+4=7, ISUP grade group 2.
Left TMJ lesion with preliminary pathologic diagnosis of calcified chondromesenchymal neoplasm.

Diffusely infiltrative multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) of the thyroid with dominant 2.5 cm left-sided mass, bilateral cervical nodal metastases, extrathyroidal extension, vascular invasion, positive margins, and soft tissue/tracheal region involvement. Disease course included persistent/recurrent locoregional nodal and soft tissue metastases and pulmonary nodules highly suspicious for metastatic disease.
Right temporal/basal ganglia/insular pilocytic astrocytoma, low-grade, with residual tumor after subtotal resection and subsequent radiologic regrowth.

Pulmonary adenocarcinoma diagnosed on axillary lymph node biopsy, with TTF-1 positivity. Clinical disease involved bilateral axillary lymph nodes, pleura, mediastinal nodes, and pulmonary consolidative lesions.

Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid with a small papillary thyroid carcinoma component; metastatic disease to lungs and central neck lymph nodes. Mediastinal nodal metastatic disease was suspected on PET imaging.
Pulmonary adenocarcinoma / non-small cell lung cancer with malignant pleural effusion, subcentimeter pulmonary nodules, and mediastinal mass.
Right renal pelvis upper tract urothelial carcinoma, high-grade, initially identified as a 2.5 cm papillary tumor on ureteroscopic evaluation.

Multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma with tall cell morphology, metastatic cervical nodal disease, gross unresected right level IV nodal disease, and pulmonary metastases. Disease was considered radioactive iodine refractory based on post-thyroidectomy iodine imaging showing uptake limited to the thyroid bed and no meaningful uptake in the residual neck mass or lung nodules.
Primary hyperparathyroidism with multigland disease. Osteopenia diagnosed in 2013, later osteoporosis. History of calcium nephrolithiasis, with last stone passed in 2023.

- Initial diagnosis: T2N0 p16-negative squamous cell carcinoma of the left palate. - First recurrence (approximately 4 years prior): recurrent squamous cell carcinoma involving the left retromolar trigone, considered contiguous with the prior primary site; pathology staged as pT4a with bone invasion and one positive lymph node; margins were negative. - Subsequent recurrence (fall of the prior year): recurrent tumor at the left retromolar trigone/adjacent posterior mandibular region in the previously operated and irradiated field.

Sacrococcygeal germ cell tumor/teratoma with recurrence and metastatic disease (pulmonary nodules, inguinal lymph node involvement, and vertebral metastatic involvement/collapse). Disease was described as stage IV.
Metastatic prostate cancer; Grade Group 3 disease.
Left lung adenocarcinoma, stage IV (T4 N2 M1a).
Cholangiocarcinoma with abdominal wall involvement and peritoneal metastatic disease; initially deemed inoperable.

Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) arising in a horseshoe kidney, centered in the isthmic/interpolar region. The case had been managed as stage V/bilateral Wilms tumor for treatment planning purposes. No distant metastases were identified on available imaging.

Recurrent right upper tract urothelial carcinoma involving the ipsilateral renal pelvis; low-grade, non-invasive disease on ureteroscopic biopsy. Prior history of right distal ureteral urothelial carcinoma, stage Ta low grade, treated in 2012.
Thyroid nodule in the posterior middle third of the thyroid, measuring 1.8 cm on ultrasound, with suspicious sonographic features. A second 1.0 cm low-risk thyroid nodule was also present.

1. Left breast invasive carcinoma, post modified radical mastectomy, pathologic stage pT2N2a; triple-negative phenotype on immunohistochemistry. 2. Left renal cell carcinoma, post radical nephrectomy, pathologic stage pT3aN0. 3. Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic subtype, pathologic stage pT1aNx. 4. Ovarian mature teratoma, post oophorectomy.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the left hypopharynx/piriform sinus, with left vocal fold paralysis. No metastatic disease was identified at presentation.
Bilateral multifocal Wilms tumor involving both kidneys.
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), frontline setting. Modified Rai stage: intermediate risk, based on lymphocytosis, splenomegaly, and adenopathy.
ALK-rearranged lung malignancy with EML4-ALK fusion and TP53 co-mutation. Neurological complication described as GBS-like demyelinating polyneuropathy/autoimmune polyneuropathy.
Multiple myeloma, relapsed/refractory after at least three prior lines of therapy.
Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma involving the right parotid/preauricular region. Regional nodal metastatic disease was present in the ipsilateral neck.

Metastatic prostate cancer with widespread nodal and hepatic metastatic disease. Obstructive uropathy requiring nephrostomy; nephrostomy-dependent single functioning kidney situation was described, with an atrophic left kidney.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with bilateral cervical nodal metastases, central neck nodal disease, and left retropharyngeal nodal metastasis. Background history of Graves’ disease diagnosed at age 18.
Penile squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-independent, clinically T2N0 at initial oncologic diagnosis.

Thyroid malignancy consisting of tall-cell variant papillary thyroid carcinoma in the thyroid with metastatic anaplastic thyroid carcinoma in a left cervical lymph node. BRAF-positive disease. Suspected bilateral pulmonary metastases.
PSMA-avid metastatic prostate cancer with bulky retroperitoneal nodal disease. Right-sided obstructive uropathy was present secondary to nodal disease.

Right renal Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma), post-neoadjuvant therapy radical nephrectomy specimen showing triphasic Wilms tumor with anaplasia; stage II disease due to extrarenal vascular invasion. Eleven sampled lymph nodes were negative.

Recurrent/residual intracranial astrocytic neoplasm involving the third ventricular and right temporal regions. Prior diagnosis in 2023 had been pyelocytic astrocytoma. Following resection in 2025, the third ventricular lesion was reported as astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 4, IDH-wild type on immunohistochemistry; the temporal lesion was reported as low-grade astrocytoma.
Metastatic prostatic adenocarcinoma with extensive nodal and osseous metastases, with calvarial and dural metastatic involvement.

Low-grade adenoid cystic carcinoma of the sinonasal/skull base region, with local extension into Meckel’s cave and the left cavernous sinus. Clinical neck status was N0. PET-CT showed no regional or distant metastatic disease.
Diffuse glioma, WHO grade 2, involving the left frontal region.

Invasive moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the left oral cavity/buccal region, clinically staged cT4b cN2b cM0. Primary tumor involved the left buccal cheek/retromolar trigone region with extension into the masticator space and infratemporal fossa, with perineural spread along the mandibular nerve to the skull base. Regional nodal disease involved left level IB and level II nodes.
Hepatocellular carcinoma involving liver segments 2 and 3, initially presumed and subsequently biopsy proven; presentation complicated by tumor rupture.
ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer.

Synchronous primary malignancies: 1. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO stage IB2. 2. Right breast invasive lobular carcinoma, grade 2, estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, HER2-negative; reported as T1 pathologic, clinical N2, M0, clinical stage IIIA.
Metastatic poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma presenting with brain metastases and patchy meningeal metastases; primary site was not identified.
Olfactory neuroblastoma involving the right nasal cavity with extension into the right orbit and intracranial parasagittal/right gyrus rectus region.

Metastatic breast carcinoma, hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative, with liver and bone metastases. Primary diagnosis in 2013 was invasive ductal carcinoma, pT2N0, grade 2, estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-negative, HER2-negative.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, subsequently characterized as RET-rearranged papillary thyroid carcinoma with features consistent with diffuse sclerosing subtype/infiltration pattern. Background Hashimoto’s thyroiditis was present in the initial surgical specimen. Subsequent Graves hyperthyroidism developed in the remaining right thyroid lobe.
Right lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma with metastatic disease involving bone and paraesophageal lymph node. ECOG performance status was 1. Comorbidity: hypertension.

Poorly differentiated insular thyroid carcinoma arising from the right thyroid lobe, locally advanced and unresectable after initial partial resection. Permanent tracheostomy was required following postoperative bilateral vocal cord palsy. Additional diagnoses included extensive uterine leiomyomatosis/fibroids, bilateral non-functioning adrenal adenomas, remote history of right nephrectomy at age 9 years for undocumented indication, and hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome due to fumarate hydratase mutation.
Clival/petroclival meningioma causing brainstem compression, left cranial nerve VI palsy, left pupillary abnormality, and cerebellar signs predominantly affecting the right side.
High-risk prostate cancer with widespread nodal metastatic disease.
Intracranial solitary fibrous tumor, WHO grade 2, involving a right parasagittal/falcine midline dural-based lesion. Recurrent disease was documented in 2025 after prior resection.

Metastatic high-risk, high-volume prostate carcinoma diagnosed in March 2023, with subsequent neuroendocrine transformation. Disease progression occurred in the prostate and iliac lymph nodes after platinum-based chemotherapy plus immunotherapy.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma, right-sided, previously staged pT2Nx status post total thyroidectomy. Subsequent ultrasound demonstrated a suspicious right level IV cervical lymph node measuring 8 mm, concerning for persistent or recurrent nodal disease.
Grade 2 sinonasal chondrosarcoma, staged as T4aN0. PET-CT showed no regional or distant metastatic disease.
- Penile squamous cell carcinoma. - HPV-positive penile squamous cell carcinoma.

Right breast invasive lobular carcinoma, stage IIIC at initial diagnosis in 2014; pathologic nodal status showed 14 metastatic lymph nodes of 16 examined after mastectomy and axillary dissection. Subsequent metastatic progression to bone in 2015 and later to liver.
Malignancy in a female patient; primary tumor type was not specified in the available clinical information.
Right breast metaplastic carcinoma, predominantly epithelial type, stage pT1cN0; papillary carcinoma of thyroid, low risk.
Cervical squamous cell carcinoma, FIGO 2018 stage IA2.
Bifrontal atypical meningioma, WHO grade 2, status post neurosurgical resection.
Grade 3 oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, located in the right frontal lobe in or very near the motor cortex/corticospinal tract region.

Multicentric medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) of the thyroid, with greatest tumor in the right lobe measuring 2.2 cm, and synchronous papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) in the left lobe; later biopsy-proven right lateral cervical lymph node metastasis from MTC.
High-grade clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney, stage II at initial surgery, with subsequent solitary pulmonary nodule in the right middle lobe.
Stage IIB cervical cancer diagnosed in 2014. Subsequent brain metastasis to the cerebellum was diagnosed in October 2014.

Metastatic well-differentiated small bowel neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2, arising in the terminal ileum, with hepatic metastases. Functional neuroendocrine tumor syndrome was present, with flushing and diarrhea.

Secondary hyperparathyroidism associated with stage 4 chronic kidney disease; hypercalcemia developed over time as renal function declined. Chronic kidney disease was attributed to long-term NSAID use. The patient was not on dialysis.

Metastatic breast carcinoma, HER2-positive, hormone receptor-negative/low-positive on serial biopsies, with skeletal metastases, nodal disease, skin recurrence, right axillary nodal involvement, and brain metastases.
Unilateral right Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) with pulmonary metastases; stage IV disease on the basis of distant lung metastases.

Metastatic differentiated thyroid carcinoma involving bone, initially identified on core biopsy of an iliac bone lesion as metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma; subsequent thyroidectomy pathology was reported as poorly differentiated thyroid cancer.
Large right occipital-parietal brain mass crossing the midline, radiographically most consistent with a high-grade primary CNS neoplasm, specifically glioblastoma multiforme.

Triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast, initially diagnosed two years earlier as stage III disease with axillary nodal involvement; subsequent metastatic recurrence involving liver and lung.
Biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma with PSA 16 and Gleason score 9 (grade group 5).
Left thyroid oncocytic carcinoma, 4 cm, widely invasive; categorized as high risk of recurrence based on initial pathology.

Localized prostate adenocarcinoma involving a right posterior peripheral zone lesion, clinically palpable on the right side. Baseline clinical stage was consistent with cT1c/T2a eligibility criteria for focal therapy registry enrollment.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma with extensive locoregional disease involving the thyroid and cervical lymph nodes, with gross invasion of adjacent aerodigestive and neurovascular structures. Disease involved both sides of the thyroid and was associated with bilateral vocal cord impaired mobility. There was residual unresected right retropharyngeal/peripharyngeal nodal disease after surgery. Imaging also raised concern for metastatic disease to bone and indeterminate pulmonary nodules.
Metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma of lung origin, ALK fusion-positive, with diffuse thoracic and nodal disease at presentation.
Glioblastoma with radiographic recurrence in the left frontal lobe.
Recurrent penile cancer with fixed bulky groin nodal mass measuring 7 cm.
Prostate adenocarcinoma, pathologic stage pT3bN0, Gleason score 4+3=7, Grade Group 3, with seminal vesicle invasion and subsequent biochemical recurrence.
Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype.

Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, clinical stage cT4 cN2 at initial staging, ER low-positive, PR low-positive, HER2-negative. After surgery, pathologic stage was ypT3 ypN3. Subsequent isolated central nervous system metastatic disease was identified in August 2015.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in a thyroglossal duct cyst/thyroglossal duct tract region.

Pancytopenia with marrow dysplasia and molecular abnormalities consistent with a myelodysplastic neoplasm/myelodysplastic syndrome phenotype. Risk stratification: IPSS-R score 2.5 (low risk); IPSS-M score 0.18 (moderate-low risk).
Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

Stage III esophageal cancer at initial diagnosis on 06 March 2025. Residual disease was documented after definitive chemoradiotherapy. Subsequent PET imaging showed response in the esophagus with a lung lesion treated as metastatic disease.

Cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma, high-grade by reported necrosis, with locoregional recurrence and pulmonary metastases. Initial outside diagnosis after prior thyroidectomy had been reported as follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma.

Case 1: Sacrococcygeal mature teratoma, subsequently with recurrent metabolically active pelvic soft-tissue lesion and markedly elevated AFP consistent with recurrence. Case 2: Sacrococcygeal yolk sac tumor with metastatic disease involving lungs/pleura, right inguinal lymph nodes, and vertebral involvement.
Autonomous thyroid nodule of the left thyroid lobe; post-operative minimally invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma.
Hepatocellular carcinoma involving essentially the entirety of the right hepatic lobe, with portal hypertension. No macrovascular invasion was described.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma involving bilateral thyroid nodules, with suspected pulmonary metastatic disease. Clinical stage was documented as cT3a N0 M1, stage IVC.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus, initially diagnosed in 2024 as stage III disease; subsequently developed recurrent metastatic disease involving the paraesophageal region and lungs.
Metastatic carcinoma stomach, initially diagnosed in 2024.

1. Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, ER-positive, HER2-positive, clinical stage IIA at initial diagnosis in late 2013. 2. Synchronous high-grade serous adenocarcinoma involving both ovaries, left fallopian tube, and omentum, FIGO stage IIIC ovarian cancer, diagnosed in 2014.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the thyroid, classical variant, well differentiated.

High-grade glioma/GBM arising from a previously lower-grade glioma, with features consistent with transformed IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglial tumor. Disease had progressed multiple times after prior treatment.
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon involving the ascending colon/hepatic flexure with bilobar liver metastases.
Endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO stage IIIC, grade 1. Diagnosis date was recorded as 1 October.
Sinonasal mucosal melanoma involving the right ethmoid region; clinical stage T3N0M0 localized disease.
RET fusion-positive solid malignancy. Tumor was described as immunologically “cold.”
Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma involving the right midface/maxillary sinus region with cutaneous lesion overlying the involved area and clinical perineural involvement of V2/infraorbital nerve.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma with heavy cervical nodal burden (N1b disease), BRAF V600E-mutated, previously treated with surgery and radioactive iodine; persistent/metastatic right retropharyngeal lymph node disease. High-risk features included extranodal extension.

Adenoid cystic carcinoma, initially staged T4N0M0. Suspected local recurrence in the ipsilateral deep nasopharyngeal/pharyngeal space approximately 15 years after initial treatment. Separate thoracic metastatic disease was present and remained stable.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma involving a solitary thyroid nodule measuring 2.5 cm.
Desmoid tumor of the right neck, first diagnosed in August 2017.
Right parietal atypical meningioma, status post surgical resection and adjuvant radiotherapy, with subsequent abnormal right hemispheric post-treatment imaging changes and recurrent midline shift.
Hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosed radiographically in the setting of cirrhosis and prior hepatitis C infection; solitary lesion.
Recurrent invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the left maxillary sinus. Prior history of T3N1 squamous cell carcinoma of the left maxillary sinus.
Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, FIGO stage IV, high-risk score 12.
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma with de novo metastatic disease to the liver.
Metastatic non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (pancreatic head primary) with bilobar liver metastases; well-differentiated NET, grade 2.

Cutaneous malignant melanoma of the right back/scapular region, initially diagnosed in November 2022, stage pT2a based on primary tumor depth 1.3 mm without ulceration; subsequent regional nodal metastatic melanoma involving the right neck, confirmed by fine-needle aspiration. PET imaging demonstrated regional disease only.
Recurrent/metastatic Hürthle cell carcinoma involving the right thyroid bed/central neck, central neck lymph nodes, and multiple intramuscular/subplatysmal soft-tissue nodules in the neck.
Hormone receptor-positive breast adenocarcinoma; HER2 immunohistochemistry 2+ with negative FISH testing. Metastatic disease was present in the sternum.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Subsequently developed acute myeloid leukemia (AML), described as therapy-associated on bone marrow biopsy and associated with very poor prognosis.
Low-grade conventional chondrosarcoma involving the pelvis/right sacral region, reported to originate from the sacral root.
WHO grade 4 astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, involving the left temporal lobe with multifocal disease.
De novo neuroendocrine small cell carcinoma arising from the prostate, with metastatic disease involving pelvic/inguinal and abdominopelvic lymph nodes.
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-related nasopharyngeal carcinoma, staged cT2N2 at initial diagnosis. Subsequent intracranial/temporal lobe process was clinically assessed as radiation necrosis rather than recurrent disease.
Intermediate-grade adenoid cystic carcinoma, initially diagnosed 4 years earlier, with subsequent metastatic recurrence.
Left thyroid nodule with preoperative left vocal fold paralysis.
Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, triple-negative, clinical stage II, cT2N0M0.
Ileal gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).

Metastatic well-differentiated thyroid carcinoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma follicular variant, with extensive distant metastatic disease involving chest wall/ribs, right atrium/superior vena cava, pleural/posterior cul-de-sac region, multiple vertebral bodies, left humeral head, spine, and iliac crest.

Osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the right distal femur, initially diagnosed in 2009. Recurrent high-grade pleomorphic spindle cell sarcoma in the right thigh/femur region in 2022, characterized as recurrent osteosarcoma. Metastatic pulmonary disease was identified on staging imaging. Segmental pulmonary embolism was diagnosed in January 2023.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma presenting with metastatic cervical, mediastinal, and pulmonary disease. Subsequent disease course included hepatic and osseous metastases.

Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / clonal B-cell lymphocytosis with bilateral axillary adenopathy. Prior history of stage I breast cancer, with no evidence of disease for approximately 15 years after treatment.
Clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney with extensive local involvement of the inferior vena cava (IVC), initially considered locally advanced and unresectable.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma with occult primary in the thyroid and metastatic right lateral cervical lymph node involvement. Pathologic stage was reported as T1a N1b. Distant metastatic status was not established.

- Initial diagnosis in 2013: right breast invasive ductal carcinoma with extensive high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), triple-negative phenotype; pathologic stage I, pT1bN0M0. - Subsequent ipsilateral right breast recurrence/new lesion in 2015: DCIS with multiple foci of microinvasive/invasive ductal carcinoma, triple-negative phenotype.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lobe lung. Clinical stage before brain MRI was described as T4N1 non-small cell lung cancer. A small brain lesion concerning for solitary metastasis was subsequently identified on MRI; stage designation under consideration included stage IIIA versus stage IVA.

Initially diagnosed with locally advanced triple-negative breast cancer, clinical stage T3N2. Subsequent disease progression with extensive bone and nodal metastases. Performance status was 1. No known comorbidities.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with cervical nodal metastases and pulmonary metastases (M1 disease). Postoperative pathology described pulmonary thyroid cancer, diffusely infiltrating.

Localised prostate adenocarcinoma, initially staged as clinical T2a, with Gleason score 4+3. Subsequent adjacent/in-field recurrence at the prostatic apex was identified on follow-up imaging after focal irreversible electroporation (IRE).

Pelvic/rectal inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor involving the rectum and anal canal, with extension to adjacent pelvic structures. Distal colonic acute intestinal obstruction had occurred at initial major hospitalization in November 2021.
Recurrent regional squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx involving the right neck. Original disease had been T4N1 laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

Cervical carcinoma, FIGO stage IIIB. Clinical examination identified an 8 cm ulcerated cervical mass with parametrial involvement. CT demonstrated extension to the lower third of the vagina and nodal disease in the common iliac and retroperitoneal regions.
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype; stage II disease.

Left renal cell carcinoma, reported as translocation-associated renal cell carcinoma (TFE3-rearranged RCC impression on immunohistochemistry), with regional nodal involvement. Pathologic stage was reported as pT3. Clinical stage IV disease was considered on the basis of mediastinal lymphadenopathy and a pulmonary nodule on imaging.

Classical variant papillary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed in 2007 with central and right lateral cervical nodal metastases. Subsequent recurrent radioiodine-refractory nodal disease was identified in the right superior mediastinum/right peritracheal region.
Low rectal adenocarcinoma without distant metastases at presentation.
Prostate adenocarcinoma, Grade Group 4.
Submandibular gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma, initially diagnosed in 2023, with subsequent metastatic disease involving brain and lungs.

Ulcerated cutaneous melanoma of the right neck, pathologic stage pT4b. Clinical satellite lesions were present at the primary site, consistent with N1c disease. No proven distant metastases were identified. Overall stage was recorded as stage IIIC.
Extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma with brain metastases and soft tissue metastasis.
Small intestine neuroendocrine tumor arising in the ileum, initially stage III based on regional nodal involvement; subsequent metastatic recurrence involving the liver and later liver and bone.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), heavily pretreated, with high-volume metastatic disease involving diffuse osseous/bone marrow metastases, bulky nodal disease, and liver metastasis.
Sacrococcygeal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.

Lynch syndrome with germline MSH2 and MSH6 mutations; history of colorectal cancer; recurrent upper tract urothelial carcinoma. Prior left upper tract urothelial carcinoma was initially high-grade and later recurred as low-grade disease. Subsequent right proximal ureteral urothelial tumor was concerning for cT3 disease.
High-grade differentiated thyroid carcinoma, pT2N0, arising in the thyroid isthmus.

Bilateral breast carcinoma, stage IV, diagnosed in 2020. Hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive disease (ER/PR positive, HER2 positive). Repeat biopsies continued to demonstrate HER2-positive disease.
Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast carcinoma with bone-only metastatic disease, diagnosed in November 2016.
Stage IV EGFR-mutated primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with metastatic involvement of mediastinal/peribronchovascular lymph nodes, liver, bone, and brain.
Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with osseous metastases.

Metastatic EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma of the left lower lobe with malignant pleural effusion; thoracic nodal metastatic disease and later brain metastasis. Initial clinical status included ECOG performance status 2, approaching 3.

Follicular thyroid carcinoma, primary tumor 1.5 cm, staged pT1b cM0 at initial diagnosis. Disease later recurred with radioactive iodine-avid pulmonary metastases and subsequently progressed with osseous and hepatic metastases.
Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
Metastatic breast carcinoma, stage IV, described in an oligometastatic setting with a spinal metastasis.

High-risk prostate adenocarcinoma status post radical prostatectomy in 2012, followed by nodal metastatic recurrence involving pelvic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes, consistent with nodal metastatic disease (N1 and M1a).
Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with ALK-EML fusion and TP53 co-mutation. Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy/Guillain-Barré syndrome-like neuropathy developed during treatment with lorlatinib.
Stage IV squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lobe of the lung at initial diagnosis.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) involving both thyroid lobes, with biopsy-proven bilateral cervical nodal metastases; metastatic pulmonary disease with diffuse bilateral miliary-pattern lung nodules/micronodules. Focal leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI was identified without cytologic confirmation on subsequent lumbar punctures.
Periampullary carcinoma, pancreatic subtype. Postoperative stage IV disease with liver metastases and multiple abdominal nodal metastases.
Hyperthyroidism associated with a right thyroid nodule. Fine-needle aspiration was diagnostic of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the breast, described as double-hit lymphoma.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma involving a right thyroid nodule measuring 1.3 cm on biopsy/imaging. Incidentally identified bilateral subcentimeter pulmonary nodules were also present.

Non-small cell lung cancer of the lung, diagnosed in July 2025. Disease was described as stage III at initial diagnosis; subsequent clinical characterization included unresectable stage III versus stage IV disease, with multiple lung nodules and oligometastatic/stage IV disease considered in the record. ALK-positive disease with EML4-ALK fusion.
Non-small cell lung carcinoma, consistent with adenocarcinoma of the right lower lobe, grade 2; clinical stage cT3N3M1 (stage IV) ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma.
Lung cancer was under evaluation. An EGFR kinase domain duplication was identified on broad genomic profiling.
Invasive squamous cell carcinoma involving the caudal septum/collumellar region with extension onto the nasal floor bilaterally.

Metastatic breast carcinoma with neuroendocrine transformation. Disease manifestations included liver metastasis with poorly differentiated high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma morphology and a separate right axillary metastasis consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma. Original breast primary was ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with bilateral thyroid involvement and bilateral cervical nodal metastases.

HER2-positive breast carcinoma with metastatic disease. Metastatic sites/documented disease involvement included skull metastases, spinal metastases with L3 compression fracture, possible/concern for cauda equina syndrome, and leptomeningeal disease. CNS crisis/brain involvement was described. Triple-positive disease was referenced.
Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, diagnosed in March 2017; grade II; ER-negative; PR-negative; HER2-positive by FISH. Chronic renal disease with compromised renal function was also documented.
Recurrent functioning pituitary macroadenoma associated with acromegalic features and elevated IGF-1.

Non-metastatic muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (transition cell carcinoma) of the urinary bladder, clinical stage cT3 with extravesical extension and transmural vesicoureteric junction involvement causing upstream left hydroureteronephrosis; cN0 cM0. Background comorbidities included Crohn’s disease, atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate, and sensorineural hearing loss.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe with multifocal disease and central compartment nodal metastases.

Multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma, including a left papillary thyroid microcarcinoma and a contralateral microscopic focus, in the setting of Hashimoto thyroiditis/hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine since 2015.

Well-differentiated papillary squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue, with possible anterior floor-of-mouth involvement and no clinical or radiographic nodal or distant metastatic disease at presentation.

Left breast ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) with microinvasion after mastectomy pathology; positive medial surgical margin. Sentinel lymph node findings showed isolated groups of neoplastic cells. Right breast showed no malignancy. BRCA mutation was reported.
Left pleural malignant mesothelioma, epithelioid subtype, with extensive left hemithoracic disease and subsequent abdominal metastatic involvement.

Prostate adenocarcinoma, initially low-risk disease diagnosed in 2015; subsequently upgraded on repeat biopsy in April 2019 to Grade Group 2, Gleason score 3+4=7, favorable intermediate-risk, left-sided disease.
Primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) / small round blue cell tumor involving the right labia majora, with pulmonary metastatic disease.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, identified after left lobectomy.

Triple-positive left breast invasive ductal carcinoma (estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, HER2-positive), presenting with fixed axillary lymphadenopathy and synchronous liver metastasis, consistent with stage IV oligometastatic breast cancer.
Metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma with bone-only metastatic disease; progression after two lines of hormonal therapy.

Multifocal infiltrative hepatocellular carcinoma involving the right hepatic lobe and lower liver, in the setting of cirrhosis secondary to previously treated hepatitis C virus infection with sustained virologic response. Child-Pugh class A6 liver function.
Left insular/temporal astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 2.
Clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney, with inferior vena cava tumor thrombus extending to the right atrium. No evidence of adenopathy was reported.
Right thyroid nodule, 4.4 cm, with indeterminate cytology (atypia of undetermined significance). Additional left thyroid spongiform nodule, 1.5 cm.
Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma in the sellar/suprasellar region with residual/recurrent disease after surgery and CyberKnife treatment.

Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, initially stage IIIB. The patient achieved a complete response after definitive chemoradiation. Five years later, recurrent disease developed in the right masticator space. Subsequent biopsy-proven recurrent disease in the nasopharynx was identified. A right temporal lobe lesion was present.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. Initial clinical stage was recorded as FIGO stage IIA2. Subsequent pelvic MRI and CT abdomen/pelvis described locally advanced cervical malignancy with parametrial involvement and suspected posterior bladder wall/base involvement. Cystoscopy was normal. In the absence of bladder mucosal involvement, disease was discussed as stage IIB if no nodal disease was present; stage IIIC would apply if lymph nodes were involved.
Right thyroid nodule, 2.0-2.4 cm, classified on ultrasound as TI-RADS 5; fine-needle aspiration cytology was Bethesda V (suspicious for malignancy).

Typical lung carcinoid (low-grade well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor) of the right lower lobe, initially resected in 2007. Subsequent recurrent/metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor involving the liver, described as bilobar hepatic metastases.
Diffuse malignant peritoneal mesothelioma, epithelioid type, initially diagnosed in 2016; subsequent biopsy-proven pleural involvement with bicavitary mesothelioma.

Widely invasive Hürthle cell (oncocytic) thyroid carcinoma, 8 cm, with gross extrathyroidal extension, positive margins, and extensive vascular invasion. Metastatic intrathoracic/mediastinal disease was present. Subsequent recurrent disease developed in the central neck bilaterally, predominantly on the right.
Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving intraparotid lymph nodes, favored to represent metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma from an unknown primary.

Right breast carcinoma diagnosed in late 2017. Invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast, no special type, hormone receptor-positive and HER2-positive. CT chest demonstrated metastatic disease with widespread osseous metastases and enlarged right intramammary and axillary nodes, consistent with metastatic breast cancer.
Carcinoma right breast, triple-negative breast cancer, stage II at diagnosis in January 2024. ECOG performance status was 1 at diagnosis.
Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4.

Metastatic follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma (FVPTC/FBPTC reported in record), with osseous and orbital metastatic disease. Documented metastatic sites included parieto-occipital scalp/calvarial lesion, temporal bone involvement, and right orbital metastasis with intracranial extension.

High-risk localized prostate cancer. Initial biopsy demonstrated Gleason score 5+5=10, Grade Group 5 adenocarcinoma. Subsequent pathology demonstrated very high-grade adenocarcinoma with possible neuroendocrine/small cell features on re-biopsy after initiation of androgen deprivation therapy.
Stage IVA squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, with extension into the posterior bladder base. Patient was COVID-19 positive at the time of initial definitive treatment.
High-grade serous carcinoma of the ovary, stage III. Diagnosis was established in October 2025.
Penile squamous cell carcinoma of the glans penis, clinically node-negative at presentation. Clinical stage was reported as cT2N0, stage IIA.
Primary hyperparathyroidism with persistent disease after prior parathyroidectomies.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, clinically staged cT1b cN1b cM0, stage IVB, with no distant metastatic disease at presentation.

Multicompartment skull base meningioma, WHO grade 1, involving the middle cranial fossa with extension into the posterior fossa, cavernous sinus region, and extracranially through the foramen ovale into the infratemporal fossa.

Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), chronic phase, Philadelphia chromosome-positive. Low-risk disease at initial diagnosis. Post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation course was complicated by chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) involving skin, gastrointestinal tract, and liver, and later by pulmonary infectious complications including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and suspected tissue-invasive CMV infection.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma with mediastinal mass and multiple-site metastases.

Poorly differentiated neoplasm/carcinoma, treated clinically as probable non-small cell lung carcinoma with suspected lung primary. Radiologic pattern was considered consistent with lymphangitic carcinomatosis.
Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, pathologic stage IIB (T2N1).
Glioblastoma, WHO grade 4.

Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma of the ventral tongue, predominantly right-sided with extension to the midline region. Final pathologic findings were consistent with node-positive oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
Undifferentiated high-grade pleomorphic sarcoma of the abdominal wall, also described as malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma diagnosed in May 2025. Stage IV disease at diagnosis with lung and liver metastases. Comorbid diabetes mellitus. ECOG/performance status 2.
Atypical meningioma, WHO grade 2.

Left breast invasive lobular carcinoma, initially staged as pT3N3a after left mastectomy, with de novo metastatic bone disease on PET-CT. Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Subsequent contralateral breast progression in May 2025 with ipsilateral axillary nodal involvement on imaging and biopsy-confirmed invasive lobular carcinoma in the opposite breast.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma involving the left thyroid lobe with cervical nodal disease.
HER2-amplified advanced/recurrent uterine serous carcinoma.

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), stage IV/metastatic in the presented cohort. Lung metastases were documented in a representative case. The cohort included patients with differing underlying etiologies of HCC; many had hepatitis B, and some had hepatitis C. Cirrhosis was described as the principal underlying risk factor for HCC in this population.
Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2, estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, clinically early stage; final pathologic tumor size 1.8 cm; sentinel lymph nodes negative.
Clival chordoma presenting as a large nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal mass with skull base, upper cervical spine, and intracranial extension.

SMARCB1-deficient sinonasal carcinoma. Initial diagnosis was biopsy proven. A first local recurrence in the right ethmoid region was biopsy proven and treated. A later recurrence was also biopsy proven and showed the same tumor type. Disease recurred locally without evidence of systemic metastatic disease at the times described.
Recurrent prostate adenocarcinoma with oligometastatic/low-volume metastatic disease involving a single hilar thoracic lymph node after prior prostatectomy and salvage radiation.
Intermediate-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor arising in the head of the pancreas, with metastatic disease to the liver and cervical lymph nodes.

Multiply recurrent intermediate-grade adenoid cystic carcinoma of the left sinonasal/maxillary region with involvement of the left orbit, pterygoid skull base region, sphenoid sinus, infratemporal fossa, and nasopharyngeal bulging; prior isolated pulmonary metastasis had been resected in 2022.

Sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma, initially diagnosed in 2016. Initial surgical stage was pT3N1bM0. Recurrent locoregional nodal disease developed postoperatively. Somatic RET-mutant disease with later oligoprogression in a right supraclavicular lymph node while on selpercatinib.
Recurrent poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma involving the left carotid space/left level II neck.
High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, FIGO stage IIIC.

Functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (gastrinoma/Zollinger-Ellison syndrome), arising from the uncinate process/head of pancreas; well-differentiated grade 3 neuroendocrine tumor with nodal and later hepatic, retroperitoneal nodal, and osseous metastatic disease.

Undiagnosed nonenhancing mass centered in the interpeduncular fossa/retroinfundibular region, located posterior to the optic chiasm and pituitary stalk and anterior to the brainstem. No tissue diagnosis had been obtained.
Transverse colon adenocarcinoma with a large locally advanced mass adherent to the anterior abdominal wall. Tumor was mismatch repair deficient / MSI-high.
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma of the ureter. The tumor was described as heterogeneous, predominantly low grade with focal high-grade areas.

Oral cavity malignancy arising in the left gingivobuccal sulcus, with rapid interval progression to direct cutaneous invasion involving the facial/submental skin and oral commissure. Disease was classified as T4a after progression with skin invasion.
High-grade serous ovarian adenocarcinoma, FIGO stage IV.
Astrocytoma, WHO grade 3.
Adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon, stage IIIC (T4a N2 M0), non-metastatic.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the supraglottic larynx involving the epiglottis. Clinical stage at presentation was cT1N0. Final pathologic stage after resection was pT3N0 due to focal cartilage involvement and pre-epiglottic space invasion.
Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, initially diagnosed in 2015 as stage III pancreatic cancer; current disease described as stage IV progressive metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

- 2011: ER-positive/PR-positive, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast with associated ductal carcinoma in situ, stage T2N1. - Metastatic recurrence identified in November with osseous involvement at T2 and hepatic metastasis. - Liver biopsy confirmed metastatic carcinoma of breast origin, ER-positive, HER2-negative (IHC 2+, HER2-low).
Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma with a locally advanced left renal primary and pulmonary metastases.
Metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), chemotherapy-naive, with multiple bone metastases.
Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with malignant right pleural effusion/pleural involvement. Disease later progressed with lumbar bone metastasis.

Poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the right lung with infiltration of the right main bronchus. Initial nodal staging by EBUS-FNAC showed station 4R positivity with stations 7 and 10 negative, consistent with cT3N2 disease.

Right adnexal mass highly suspicious for ovarian malignancy with omental involvement and small-volume ascites; advanced-stage intra-abdominal malignancy was suspected clinically. Pathologic confirmation had not been obtained.
Inferior vena cava mass identified in summer 2024; high-grade sarcoma on catheter-based intraluminal biopsy pathology.

Metastatic high-grade thyroid carcinoma. Outside neck mass biopsy had reportedly shown poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Subsequent pathology from tracheostomy/isthmus specimen was reported as high-grade oncocytic thyroid carcinoma; morphologic description was consistent with poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Disease involved the neck with extensive distant metastatic spread, including osseous metastases.
Hepatoblastoma involving both lobes of the liver; staged as PRETEXT III, standard risk.

Prostate adenocarcinoma, initially localized to the right peripheral zone, Gleason score 3+4 on initial biopsy. Subsequent residual/recurrent clinically significant disease was confirmed on repeat targeted biopsy as Gleason score 4+3 in the right side. Additional low-volume Gleason score 3+3 disease was identified in the left posterior prostate.
Right distal ureter high-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma with regional lymph node involvement; clinical stage cTx N2 M0. Chronic kidney disease stage 3 was present at diagnosis.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe.
Localized prostate adenocarcinoma.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with bulky locoregional nodal metastases. Structural distant metastatic disease to the lungs was present.
Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

ER-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer of invasive lobular histology, initially diagnosed in 2022 as locally advanced breast cancer and subsequently found to have osseous metastatic disease.
Metastatic parathyroid carcinoma with liver metastases and subsequent pulmonary metastases; associated refractory hypercalcemia due to hyperparathyroidism.
Primary hyperparathyroidism, described in the record as normocalcemic hyperparathyroidism.
Lung adenocarcinoma involving the left lower lobe, with pleural effusion and pleural fluid cytology positive for malignant cells.
Locally advanced basal cell carcinoma of the left cheek/left lateral zygomatic-temporal region; clinical stage T3N0M0.
Metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor involving the pancreatic tail with liver metastases.
- Primary hyperparathyroidism. - Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe, tall cell subtype, multifocal, with nodal metastasis.

Primary breast diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), stage IIE at initial diagnosis, with subsequent right axillary nodal relapse and later secondary central nervous system lymphoma involving the brain parenchyma.

Type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney, initially stage pT1a, with subsequent ipsilateral renal recurrence (pT1b), metastatic involvement of the right adrenal gland, bilateral adrenal/adrenal fossa recurrence, and later para-aortic renal fossa recurrence.

Olfactory neuroblastoma (esthesioneuroblastoma) of the left sinonasal cavity with skull base invasion, intracranial extension, meningeal/dural enhancement, and cervical nodal metastasis. Staged as Kadish D. Neck disease was identified on CT neck as a positive left cervical lymph node.
Pituitary adenoma, initially diagnosed as pituitary microadenoma approximately 6 years earlier.
High-grade papillary serous carcinoma of the ovary, initially diagnosed in September 2021; stage III at initial diagnosis.

Malignant peritoneal mesothelioma. Initial biopsy diagnosis was epithelioid mesothelioma. In a separate but otherwise similar case described for comparison, final pathology after resection demonstrated sarcomatoid/biphasic histology.
Stage IV / extensive-stage large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, managed clinically as small cell carcinoma.
Metastatic right-sided colon adenocarcinoma with peritoneal metastases and bladder dome involvement; BRAF V600E-mutated, microsatellite-stable disease.
Primary hyperparathyroidism.

Recurrent multifocal high-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) involving the contralateral solitary kidney, with disease in the renal pelvis and proximal ureter. Prior urothelial cancer history included high-grade Ta non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer diagnosed in 2019, subsequent bladder carcinoma in situ, and right-sided high-grade UTUC treated surgically in 2022.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed at age 3 years, with metastatic disease involving lungs, pleura, and bone. Disease was radioactive iodine-refractory at the time of referral based on a negative whole-body scan despite progressive metastatic disease, and later demonstrated some restored iodine uptake after RET inhibitor therapy.

Recurrent right oral tongue squamous neoplasia, including well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma and multiple episodes of carcinoma in situ/dysplasia. Initial stage was documented as T1N0 in 2011. A recurrent invasive lesion in 2018 was documented as T1.

Recurrent muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder; prior outside TURBT had shown high-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma. Subsequent evaluation demonstrated recurrent disease staged radiologically as at least cT3N0.

Known right breast carcinoma, invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 3. Subsequently developed a left frontal brain metastasis from breast primary. Metastatic disease was also identified in the L5 and D10 vertebral bodies and in axillary and mediastinal lymph nodes.

Urothelial bladder cancer initially diagnosed in 2019, previously treated with intravesical BCG. Disease progressed in 2021 to muscle-invasive bladder cancer with a large bladder mass and metastatic retroperitoneal and pelvic adenopathy.

Multifocal IDH-wildtype diffuse glioma of the right insular/right frontal region, subsequently classified as molecular glioblastoma based on molecular features. Later multifocal progression involved the right frontal region and a left parietal lesion.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the right mandibular alveolus/gingiva.
Stage IV pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor arising from the pancreatic tail with liver metastases.
Metastatic low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, presumed midgut/small bowel primary, with mesenteric mass and hepatic metastases. Carcinoid syndrome symptoms were present.
Localized recurrent prostate adenocarcinoma following prior HDR brachytherapy monotherapy and subsequent focal HIFU hemiablation.
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the descending colon (stage IV) with liver metastases, peritoneal/omental deposits, and pericolic nodal disease.
Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with massive pleural effusion and bone metastases at presentation.
Widely invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma of the thyroid, AJCC stage pT3aN0, stage II; high risk of recurrence. Disease subsequently demonstrated pulmonary metastatic involvement on FDG PET/CT.

Acute myeloid leukemia with monocytic differentiation. Peripheral blood smear and bone marrow morphology showed monoblasts/promonocytes. Bone marrow was hypercellular. Cytogenetics showed a normal female karyotype.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma with sarcomatoid features on fine-needle aspiration of a right thyroid mass; metastatic disease was present on PET imaging.
Metastatic right breast carcinoma, hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative, with nodal and osseous metastases.
Right frontal diffuse astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 2.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma, partially resected at initial surgery, with gross residual tumor in the left thyroid bed and tracheal invasion/submucosal tracheal involvement. Tumor had been incidentally identified after CT chest/abdomen performed for rib pain demonstrated a thyroid mass.

Stage IV well-differentiated low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, presumed small bowel primary, metastatic to liver and mesenteric lymph nodes, with carcinoid syndrome. Subsequent carcinoid heart disease was documented with tricuspid valve involvement.
Stage III triple-negative breast carcinoma.

Post-cystectomy left ureteral urothelial carcinoma, clinically concerning for locally advanced upper tract disease (radiographically concerning for T3 disease), without evidence of metastatic disease at presentation.
Small renal mass of the right kidney without metastatic disease.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed by fine-needle aspiration of an isthmic thyroid nodule (Bethesda VI).
Left hypoglossal canal dumbbell-shaped lesion, radiologically favored to represent a hypoglossal schwannoma.
Metastatic renal malignancy with a large left renal primary tumor and metastatic disease involving bilateral adrenal glands and lung.
Colon adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon; pathologic stage pT3N0 (stage II).
Lung adenocarcinoma with concurrent left pleural effusion/hemorrhagic pleural fluid and coexistent isoniazid-monoresistant pleural tuberculosis.
Metastatic TTF1-positive poorly differentiated carcinoma consistent with primary lung malignancy.
Metastatic cancer with reported high microsatellite instability (MSI-high). Prostate cancer was referenced in relation to a pathognomonic ERG fusion.
Metastatic gastric carcinoma, stage IV at initial presentation; MSI-high; HER2-negative; PD-L1 expression approximately 5-10%.
Rectal well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid) with liver-only metastatic disease.
Recurrent adenoid cystic carcinoma involving the frontal sinus/frontal bone with extension into the left orbit. Prior malignancy had been diagnosed in 1998; recurrence had been treated in 2006.
Cervical squamous cell carcinoma, FIGO stage IIB.
Posterior fossa ependymoma centered in the fourth ventricle; histologically WHO grade 3.

Left upper lobe lung squamous cell carcinoma, initially staged cT4N0M0; postoperative pathologic stage pT4N0. Subsequent isolated endotracheal recurrence was identified approximately 1 year after initial treatment.
Multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, classified as late BCLC-B stage.
Gastric adenocarcinoma, status post radical subtotal gastrectomy, with subsequent progressive metastatic gastric cancer.
Persistent primary hyperparathyroidism after prior unsuccessful right-sided parathyroid exploration/parathyroidectomy.
- Initial diagnosis in 2016: left orbital plasmacytoma. - Subsequent diagnosis after recurrence workup: plasmablastic lymphoma involving the left orbital/upper eyelid region.
Epithelioid peritoneal mesothelioma with peritoneal and omental implants along the diaphragm. Disease later progressed with lung involvement.
Right frontal astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, WHO grade 2.
Incidentally detected pancreatic tail lesion, diagnosed on biopsy as a well-differentiated low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
Diffuse peritoneal epithelioid mesothelioma.

Multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma status post prior total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection, with recurrent/persistent disease in the left central neck and biopsy-proven pulmonary metastases.

Giant pituitary macroadenoma with sellar and suprasellar extension, associated obstructive hydrocephalus and visual pathway compression. Intratumoral hemorrhagic change/apoplexy was present at surgery.

Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), initially presenting as diffuse nodal disease with bone marrow involvement. At relapse, repeat biopsy was consistent with more aggressive pleomorphic, if not blastoid, mantle cell lymphoma.

Synchronous gynecologic malignancies diagnosed in March 2025: - Ovarian carcinoma, stage III, involving the left ovary. - Endometrial carcinoma, stage IA. ECOG performance status was 1. Comorbidities included type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Family history was positive for endometrial cancer in the mother and maternal aunt.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe, tall cell variant, with extrathyroidal extension and metastatic cervical lymph node involvement (right central and right lateral neck).

- Toxic multinodular goiter diagnosed at age 63. - Recurrent hyperthyroidism approximately 16 years after prior radioactive iodine treatment. - Left thyroid nodule with initial fine-needle aspiration reported as Bethesda category III, atypical cells of undetermined significance.
Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, Revised International Staging System (R-ISS) stage II. High-risk disease due to t(4;14). Transplant-eligible.
Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney with osseous metastases.

Recurrent/persistent squamous cell carcinoma of the glottic larynx involving the anterior commissure after prior endoscopic treatment and definitive radiotherapy. Initial disease had arisen in the right true vocal fold with extension to the anterior commissure and involvement near the right arytenoid/vocal process.
Triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast, clinical stage T1N1, grade 3. Germline BRCA1 mutation carrier.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic variant, arising in the right thyroid lobe, with bilateral cervical nodal metastases.
Pineal region/posterior tectal plate extra-axial lesion; radiologic impression favored epidermoid cyst. History of obstructive hydrocephalus requiring VP shunt insertion in 2005.

Multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid, primary tumor size 4.2 cm, initially staged as intermediate-risk pT3a N1b. Subsequently developed radioactive iodine-refractory, biochemically persistent and structurally recurrent locoregional metastatic disease involving pretracheal/Delphian nodal tissue, subcutaneous peri-incisional soft tissue, sternocleidomastoid muscle, thyroid bed, strap muscle, paratracheal nodes, and cervical lymph nodes. No distant metastatic disease was identified.

Cervical adenocarcinoma, grade 2, identified on biopsy from a cervical growth. Clinical examination showed a broad, barrel-shaped cervix with cervical ectropion and an ulcerated growth measuring approximately 5–6 cm on the posterior lip of the cervix. Bimanual and rectovaginal examination found both parametria free and all fornices free. MRI demonstrated a cervical lesion with stromal ring disruption and extension into the parametrium/left broad ligament. Primary site distinction between cervix and endometrium remained unresolved on available data.
Advanced liver cancer with extrahepatic spread to lymph node(s).

Locally invasive metastatic poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (insular form), with mediastinal nodal metastases, pulmonary metastases, and tumor thrombus involving the right internal jugular vein.

- History of colon cancer resected in 2015, stage pT3N0. - Subsequent metastatic adenocarcinoma involving the lung, with biopsy showing intestinal differentiation and immunophenotype suggestive of colorectal origin. - Concurrent pancreatic head/periampullary mass was present on imaging. - MSI status was stable.
Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), diagnosed in April 2024. Recurrent disease was identified on 19 December 2025. Re-excision specimen showed recurrent high-grade glioma.

Left breast carcinoma, clinically operable. Initial clinical findings were a 4 cm lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast with a single mobile left axillary lymph node measuring 1.5 cm. Clinical stage details were not otherwise specified.
Localized renal cell carcinoma of the kidney; postoperative diagnosis was clear cell renal cell carcinoma, pathologic stage pT1a.
Locally advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma involving the thyroid, trachea, and cricoid, with gross extrathyroidal extension.

Left renal mass consistent with locally advanced renal malignancy. In a separate metastatic presentation, there was a locally advanced left renal tumor with bilateral pulmonary nodules and multiple hypervascular liver nodules concerning for metastatic disease.
Left hypoglossal canal dumbbell-shaped lesion, radiologically favored to represent a hypoglossal schwannoma.
Merkel cell carcinoma of the left ear with additional left upper neck cutaneous Merkel cell carcinoma and metastatic involvement of the left parotid lymph nodes. Reported stage was stage IIIA.
D7 spinal anastomosing hemangioma with cord compression; residual disease remained after decompressive surgery.

Multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of hepatitis C-related chronic liver disease/cirrhosis. Symptomatic left skull base/sellar-region lesion involving the pituitary, sphenoid sinus, and cavernous sinus, with differential not histologically confirmed at the time of reporting.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, stage IVC, with pulmonary metastatic disease.
Left breast invasive lobular carcinoma, stage IB, pT1c pN1mi M0.

Cervical squamous cell carcinoma, stage IB2 at initial diagnosis. Subsequent progressive disease with parametrial infiltration after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, followed later by pulmonary metastatic progression.

Olfactory neuroblastoma with left cervical nodal metastasis, initially diagnosed in 2013; Kadish stage D; Dulguerov stage T4N1. Recurrent metastatic disease identified in 2025 involving bilateral cervical lymph nodes and sacrum.

Prostate adenocarcinoma, initially diagnosed in September 2011 as Gleason score 3+4=7 disease involving 3 of 12 biopsy cores, with presenting PSA 6 ng/mL. Biopsy-confirmed local recurrence was identified in 2018 as bilateral Gleason score 4+3=7 prostate cancer with PSA 3.6 ng/mL. Subsequent biochemical recurrence occurred after salvage cryotherapy.

Follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, with central compartment lymph node metastasis showing extranodal extension. Additional papillary thyroid microcarcinomas were identified in the right thyroid lobe after completion thyroidectomy.

Locally advanced breast carcinoma, clinical stage cT4bN2 at presentation. Post-mastectomy pathologic stage ypT3N2. Disease remained locoregionally confined on imaging, with no distant metastasis identified.
Incidentally detected right renal mass.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid.
Prostate adenocarcinoma, Grade Group 1 (Gleason score 3+3), initially identified in 2020 on biopsy.

Cutaneous melanoma of the left postauricular scalp/skin. Initial primary tumor was staged as T3a (stage IIA) on biopsy. Subsequent surgical pathology demonstrated microsatellites and regional nodal metastases in sentinel lymph nodes, with additional non-sentinel nodal involvement after completion lymphadenectomy.

Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma of the right neck/thyroid region with locoregional invasion and distant metastatic disease. Coexisting bilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma was identified in the surgical specimen. A sigmoid colon lesion was identified on evaluation and biopsy showed adenoma with high-grade dysplasia.

Metastatic breast carcinoma, bilateral breast involvement, hormone receptor-positive and initially HER2-low by prior biopsy. Disease had involved bilateral breasts, cervical/supraclavicular and bilateral axillary lymph nodes, lungs, and bones. Left breast disease had been described as inflammatory at initial presentation; right breast disease had involved the retroareolar region with skin involvement.

Initially diagnosed in 2010 with triple-positive breast cancer (ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-positive). Metastatic recurrence/progression was documented in 2014 with bone metastases. Subsequent metastatic progression involved lung, adrenal gland, and liver. On later biopsy of a liver lesion, the tumor remained ER-positive, became PR-negative, and was HER2-negative.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe with nodal metastases, including a metastatic left level II cervical lymph node.
Metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma, ER-negative, consistent with primary lung origin, with pulmonary and osseous metastases.
Bilateral fallopian tube malignancy reported as suspicious for low-grade serous carcinoma. Abdominal wall lesion was reported as abscess formation. Uterus remained in situ following surgery.

Multifocal left upper tract urothelial carcinoma involving the ureteropelvic junction, mid ureter, and distal ureter in a solitary kidney; clinical stage was described as high-grade Tx with possible lamina propria invasion, consistent with possible cT1 disease. Concurrent active/recurrent bladder carcinoma in situ persisted after prior intravesical BCG induction.

Stage IVB metastatic lung carcinoma, suspected right lung primary, with brain, pulmonary, mediastinal nodal, left adrenal, and T8 vertebral metastases. Intracranial disease was symptomatic with mass effect from dominant right frontal and right parietal lesions.
Merkel cell carcinoma of the left auricle. Initial pathologic stage was T1N1a with clinically occult regional nodal metastasis, consistent with stage III disease.

Extensive unresectable small bowel/peritoneal malignancy with high intra-abdominal tumor burden. Disease was initially considered not amenable to surgical resection and treatment was undertaken with palliative intent.
Multinodular thyroid disease/goiter; germline pathogenic PTEN mutation consistent with Cowden syndrome/PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome.
Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe.

Persistent primary hyperparathyroidism with ectopic left parathyroid adenoma in a retrocarotid location at the thoracic inlet. Postoperative pharyngeal injury with pharyngocutaneous fistula following prior attempted left parathyroidectomy.
Right renal mass with presumed metastatic disease to the sacrum.

Right parietal anaplastic meningioma, WHO grade 3, status post craniotomy and gross total resection in August 2022, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. Subsequent follow-up imaging demonstrated a deep right-sided/corpus callosal ring-enhancing lesion with diffuse borders and extensive bilateral periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensity within the post-radiotherapy interval.
Carcinoma endometrium, stage IV, with metastatic recurrence involving the lungs. Comorbid diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present.

Pathologically confirmed intra-abdominal/pelvic malignancy with disease involving the pelvis and multiple gastrointestinal structures; disease was considered for cytoreductive surgery with intraperitoneal chemotherapy.
Unresectable metastatic penile squamous cell carcinoma.
Primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia and inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone level; osteoporosis.

Poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma involving the left ethmoid/anterior sinonasal region with extension toward the lacrimal sac/orbit; staged clinically as T4aN0 sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
Invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast, grade 3, estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, with de novo stage IV disease.
Elevated prostate-specific antigen with PI-RADS 2 multiparametric MRI and a focal PSMA-avid lesion in the left transition zone.
Large left chest/neck mass with mediastinal involvement causing tracheal deviation and respiratory compromise; tissue diagnosis was pending at the time of reporting.
Stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, adenocarcinoma subtype, with disease localized to the left pleura and malignant left pleural effusion.
Metastatic colon cancer diagnosed in October 2024, described as upper-end metastatic colon cancer. Metastatic sites documented in lung, liver, sigmoid colon, and brain.
De novo metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma with extensive nodal and osseous metastatic disease.

Non-cirrhotic, biopsy-proven hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Initial presentation was a solitary LR-5 lesion in segment 7. Subsequent recurrence presented as a 26 mm hepatic lesion on the contralateral side.
p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of the left base of tongue with ipsilateral cervical nodal metastases.
HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma of the right palatine tonsil with metastatic right cervical lymph node involvement.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe, initially classic type with gross extrathyroidal extension into strap muscles and positive margins after partial resection; subsequent completion total thyroidectomy demonstrated a 5 cm papillary thyroid carcinoma with focal oncocytic and tall cell morphology, strap muscle invasion, and microscopic central neck nodal metastasis with extranodal extension. Later right lateral neck recurrence/metastatic disease showed high-grade transformation, with pathology described as at least poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma and probably anaplastic transformation.

Metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma, stage IV at diagnosis in 2024. Date of diagnosis: 22 April 2024. Prior history of soft palate malignancy treated in 2007, with subsequent pathology reported as adenoid cystic carcinoma.

Differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma arising from the right thyroid lobe, with cervical nodal metastases, brain metastases, and subsequent pulmonary metastases. Initial clinical staging was cT3bN1bM0 before detection of intracranial metastatic disease.
Rectal adenocarcinoma with metastatic disease (stage IV), with liver and lung metastases on PET-CT.

Metastatic triple-negative breast carcinoma diagnosed in 2022, arising as a genomically distinct second primary from a prior left breast cancer. Prior breast cancer in 2019 had been ER-positive, PR-negative, HER2-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast.
Metastatic follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma with osseous, pulmonary, and later intracranial metastatic disease. Initial presentation in October 2020 with a thoracic vertebral/rib mass.

- 2017: Left ovarian borderline serous tumor following cystectomy. - May 2020: Right ovarian high-grade papillary serous cystadenocarcinoma, surgical stage IA. - December 2021: Recurrent disease 14 months after completion of adjuvant chemotherapy.
Pancreatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with liver-predominant metastatic disease. Tumor grade increased from grade 2 to grade 3 on repeat liver biopsy.
Localized pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor involving the head/uncinate process of the pancreas.
Atypical meningioma, WHO grade 2, involving the right temporal skull base/middle fossa with residual and subsequently progressive/recurrent disease after surgery and stereotactic radiosurgery.

Nevoid melanoma of the scalp. Initial pathologic stage after excisional biopsy was pT2a Nx Mx. Final stage after wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy was pT2a N2a Mx, stage IIIA melanoma.
Recurrent squamous cell carcinoma involving the left nasal cavity/maxilla/orbit region. Original diagnosis in 2021 was nasal cavity squamous cell carcinoma, p16-positive.
Right facial primitive small round cell tumor consistent with embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma on biopsy.

Salivary ductal carcinoma, initially presenting as a right neck mass in 2016. Disease later recurred with mediastinal adenopathy in 2017 and pulmonary metastatic recurrence in August 2022. Most recent biopsy in September confirmed recurrent disease.
Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lip/gingivolabial sulcus, p16-negative.
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), solitary lesion, biopsy proven.
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma involving the left retromolar trigone/mandibular region, with clinical evidence of mandibular invasion and inferior alveolar/mental nerve involvement.
Stage IV prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosed in 2016, with osseous metastatic disease. Subsequent castration-resistant progressive metastatic disease was documented.

Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity/oropharyngeal region, involving the retromolar trigone, posterior buccal mucosa, posterior maxilla, lateral pharynx, mandible, and tongue. Clinical stage based on imaging was cT4b cN2c cM0.
Stage II colon adenocarcinoma diagnosed in 2017, subsequently recurrent/metastatic disease with biopsy-proven chest wall metastasis and a PET-avid suspicious right upper quadrant abdominal mass.

- Left abdominal wall desmoid-type fibromatosis diagnosed in November 2019. - Right abdominal wall desmoid-type fibromatosis identified in 2023/2024, anatomically separate from the prior left-sided lesion.
Rectal adenocarcinoma, initially localized at first presentation; subsequently recurrent stage IV disease with unresectable bilateral lung metastases.
Cervical squamous cell carcinoma, grade 2, clinically stage IIB at initial presentation, with a synchronous malignant right ovarian/adnexal tumor reported on core biopsy as serous cystadenocarcinoma.

Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma arising from follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma, with bilateral thyroid involvement. Subsequent biochemical and radiologic recurrence/metastatic disease involving pulmonary nodules and suspected cervical nodal disease.

No personal malignancy was documented. Familial cancer predisposition evaluation was undertaken because of a family history of breast cancer and ovarian cancer. A pathogenic heterozygous BRCA1 mutation had been identified in one affected second-degree relative. The patient’s own germline testing identified a BRCA2 variant of uncertain significance (VUS).
Recurrent carcinoma of the tongue with advanced locoregional disease. Current biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma.
High-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the right parotid gland with oncocytic features.

High-grade salivary ductal carcinoma of the deep lobe of the right parotid gland with clinical inferior alveolar nerve involvement; clinical stage IVA. Disease later progressed in the right mandible without documented distant metastases.

Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney with osseous metastasis to the left iliac/acetabular region, mediastinal/subcarinal nodal metastasis, and subsequent right cerebellar brain metastasis. Pathologic stage after nephrectomy was pT2 Nx M1.

Bilateral papillary renal cell carcinoma, type 1. Pathologic stage after staged bilateral partial nephrectomies: right renal tumor pT1b; left renal tumor pT1a. Subsequent nodal recurrence/metastatic disease in the left renal hilar/retroperitoneal lymph nodes, biopsy-proven metastatic papillary type 1 renal cell carcinoma.
Metastatic carcinoma breast; hormone receptor-positive (ER/PR-positive), HER2-negative.
Stage IV well-differentiated small bowel neuroendocrine tumor with liver metastases and carcinoid syndrome.
Right frontal intra-axial brain lesion, radiologically consistent with glioma. Intraoperative frozen section favored low-grade glioma. Final histopathology was pending.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with diffuse osseous metastatic disease, nodal metastatic disease, and a subtle liver lesion on functional imaging.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma, hobnail subtype, with extensive cervical and mediastinal nodal metastases, diffuse left lung involvement with a lymphangitic pattern, and subsequent osseous metastasis in the right ninth rib. Disease was metastatic and clinically aggressive at presentation.

Hepatocellular carcinoma arising in a cirrhotic liver. Initial disease involved a dominant left hepatic lobe lesion with several additional subcentimeter hepatic lesions. Disease later progressed to multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma.
Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, grade II, triple-negative by immunohistochemistry; clinical stage IIA breast cancer.
Prostate adenocarcinoma with biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy and subsequent salvage treatment.
Renal cell carcinoma of the kidney with inferior vena cava thrombus. Disease had poor-risk features based on at least two abnormal laboratory parameters. There was no metastatic disease on workup.

Large right renal tumor, initially diagnosed as non-metastatic right Wilms tumor. Postoperative pathology was reported as unclassified malignant spindle cell sarcoma/malignant mesenchymal tumor of the kidney, with external review favoring clear cell sarcoma of the kidney. Final documented diagnostic consideration remained between Wilms tumor and clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.
Colon carcinoma, stage III at initial diagnosis. Progressive disease was documented after adjuvant chemotherapy, with new supraclavicular and mediastinal nodal disease.
Nodular melanoma of the left temporal scalp with regional metastatic disease to left parotid/preauricular and cervical lymph nodes; clinical stage pT2b cN2b, stage III locally advanced melanoma.
High-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma, clinically at least T1 at presentation.
Myeloid sarcoma presenting as extramedullary abdominal/pelvic masses without morphologic evidence of acute leukemia in the bone marrow.
Stage III colon adenocarcinoma; pathological stage pT3N1. Microsatellite-stable disease.
Left renal pelvis upper tract urothelial carcinoma (high-grade), with regional retroperitoneal nodal involvement at presentation.

Inoperable pulmonary artery sarcoma with peripheral lung nodules/lung metastases. The lesion was described as an intraluminal pulmonary artery mass; intimal sarcoma was considered in the differential classification.
