Biochemical primary hyperparathyroidism.

Oncocytic (Hürthle cell) thyroid carcinoma. Concurrent chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) had also been diagnosed in 2017. Recurrent disease had involved the thyroid bed/neck soft tissues, including scar/subcutaneous tissue, skeletal muscle, and left paratracheal region.

Widely metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, suspected small bowel primary. Clinical features and imaging favored terminal ileum or right-sided colon origin. Hepatic metastatic disease was present.

Follicular thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe with capsular and lymphovascular invasion; subsequent iodine-avid pulmonary metastatic disease. Later disease progression included bone metastasis. Refractory hypothyroidism after thyroidectomy was documented, with persistently elevated TSH despite levothyroxine therapy.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the right buccal mucosa. Disease involved the masticator space, masseter muscle, and infratemporal fossa, extending to the high infratemporal fossa. Clinical nodal disease was absent on examination. Radiologically, bilateral level IB and II lymph nodes were present. Disease was described as T4b with N2c nodal status.

Right deep hemispheric intracranial mass lesion, radiologically described as a well-circumscribed solid-cystic lesion centered in the right subcortical region/basal ganglia-thalamic region, with mass effect on the ipsilateral lateral ventricle and brainstem compression. Tissue diagnosis had not yet been finalized.

Medullary thyroid carcinoma involving bilateral thyroid lobes with cervical lymph node metastases, multiple liver metastases, and pheochromocytoma. Left vocal cord paralysis was present. No parathyroid disease was identified.

Prostate adenocarcinoma, initially high-risk by biopsy (Gleason 9), clinically localized on PSMA PET without nodal or osseous metastatic disease; status post radical prostatectomy. Final surgical pathology demonstrated Gleason score 4+3=7 with tertiary pattern 5 (Grade Group 3) and extraprostatic extension.
Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, no special type, grade 3, diagnosed in November 2017. Disease was described clinically as locally advanced and inoperable at initial surgical assessment.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe with tall cell variant features and tumor necrosis; metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma to a right level IV cervical lymph node.

Triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast, final pathologic stage III at initial diagnosis; subsequent metastatic recurrent triple-negative breast cancer involving liver and bone in 2019.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, diagnosed on fine-needle aspiration cytology in May 2017.
Ewing sarcoma of the thigh with pulmonary metastases at initial diagnosis; later developed a skull lesion consistent with relapsed/progressive disease.

Differentiated high-grade oncocytic (Hürthle cell) thyroid carcinoma, 2.0 cm primary in the left thyroid lobe, widely invasive, with extensive angiolymphatic invasion and nodal metastases. Disease subsequently became radioactive iodine-refractory and metastatic, with recurrent cervical disease, liver metastasis, pulmonary metastases, and osseous metastasis at T3. The patient had Wilcox-Dubetz syndrome.

Neurofibromatosis type 1 with giant plexiform neurofibroma involving the lateral neck, bilateral occipital regions, and right temporoparietal scalp/head region, associated with marked craniovertebral junction and upper cervical spine deformity.

1. Right true vocal fold squamous cell carcinoma, extending from the vocal process posteriorly to the anterior commissure and involving the saccule. 2. Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe, with extrathyroidal extension and regional nodal metastases. 3. Right vocal fold paralysis/immobility documented after initial biopsy.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, microcarcinoma, pathologic stage pT4aN1a. Disease involved the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and superficially invaded the esophagus.
Adenocarcinoma, grade 3, with metastatic disease manifested by pleural/pericardial effusions and a hepatic focal lesion.

Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary at presentation, subsequently localized to the tongue base. Cervical nodal metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving a right level II lymph node.

Non-small cell lung cancer, classified as poorly differentiated pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Molecular interpretation described non-small cell lung cancer with SMARCA4 alteration/deficiency and very high tumor mutational burden.
Cholangiocarcinoma.
Prostate adenocarcinoma, status post robotic radical prostatectomy, with subsequent biochemical recurrence and suspected solitary osseous metastatic recurrence.
Right thyroid oncocytic carcinoma, 8.0 cm, status post total thyroidectomy.

Locally advanced invasive vulvar cancer diagnosed in October 2019. FIGO stage III at the time of starting radiotherapy. Subsequent recurrent/metastatic disease involving the left inguinal lymph node was confirmed later in follow-up.
Left glottic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, staged as T1a.
Right pleural mesothelioma.
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), diagnosed by peripheral blood flow cytometry.

- Severe hyperparathyroidism with multigland parathyroid hyperplasia. - Papillary thyroid carcinoma with multifocal thyroid involvement and nodal metastases, including central neck and deep mediastinal nodal disease. - Chronic renal failure secondary to lithium toxicity in a solitary kidney; status post renal transplant in March 1994, with recurrent graft dysfunction/incipient renal failure by 2019. - Severe osteoporosis. - Bipolar affective disorder.
Large third ventricular mass causing obstructive hydrocephalus. The lesion extended from the anterior to posterior third ventricle. Tissue diagnosis had not yet been established.
Multifocal bilobar hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) without cirrhosis, presenting with ruptured hepatic tumor.
Cervical squamous carcinoma, clinically staged as stage IIB. Extension studies were negative.
Right glottic squamous cell carcinoma, staged as cT2N0.

Follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe, pathologic stage I (TNM stated as stage 1). Risk stratification was described as intermediate to high risk due to vascular invasion.
Triple-negative carcinoma of the left breast, staged as T4b N2 M1, with multiple pulmonary metastases.

Melanoma, initially diagnosed in 2012 after excision of a lesion on the foot/dorsum of foot. Metastatic recurrence was identified in January 2025 with abdominal nodal masses, inguinal nodal disease, and lytic bone metastases. Subsequent pathology from recurrent disease was reported as metastatic melanoma; an inguinal node biopsy was also obtained. One account described recurrent disease as amelanotic melanoma; subtype classification was otherwise not documented.
Poorly differentiated high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, primary site not identified.
Vaginal mucosal melanoma, initially diagnosed in March 2024, with subsequent locoregional recurrence and multiple liver metastases.

Poorly differentiated invasive rectal adenocarcinoma with synchronous liver-only metastatic disease. Locally advanced low rectal cancer with involvement of the right puborectalis muscle and suspected mesorectal nodal disease.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.

Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the left temple with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving the left parotid, favored to represent intraparotid metastasis. Initial stage was documented as cTxN2bM0.
Endometrial adenocarcinoma, FIGO stage I. Grade 3 tumor. Classified as high-intermediate risk.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), limited-stage disease; stage IA, revised IPI score 0.

Regional metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma involving the right parotid gland and cervical lymph nodes, in the setting of a prior right temple cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma treated with Mohs surgery.
Known acute myeloid leukemia. Intracranial lesion in the left frontal region was diagnosed on biopsy as myeloid sarcoma, consistent with CNS relapse of prior acute myeloid leukemia.

Low-grade acinic cell carcinoma of the left parotid gland with parapharyngeal extension. The disease was multiply locally recurrent despite surgery and repeated radiotherapy. He later developed distant osseous metastasis to the manubrium/sternum. Recurrent disease at tertiary evaluation was associated with mandibular osteoradionecrosis and condylar fracture.
Triple-negative breast cancer, initially early stage after pregnancy, with subsequent metastatic recurrence. Metastatic disease included lung nodules and a brain lesion.
Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-mutant.
Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma, grade group 5, Gleason score 10.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the thyroid with nodal metastases in the central neck.

- Prior diagnosis in 2021: adenocarcinoma of the cervix. - Current metastatic disease involving the lung. - Current metastatic lesion had been regarded histopathologically as a poorly differentiated or undifferentiated malignant neoplasm with uncertain primary site.
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of pancreatobiliary origin with uncertain primary site; imaging suggested possible gallbladder or bile duct primary. Liver metastases were present at diagnosis.
Multifocal papillary thyroid microcarcinoma of the right thyroid lobe; low-risk disease without extrathyroidal extension or lymph node metastasis.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe with regional nodal metastases.
Appendiceal carcinoma with local-regional peritoneal studding/implants, nodal metastases, and positive peritoneal washings.
Stage IB squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix.
Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with widespread metastatic disease.

Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma with extensive cervical and mediastinal nodal involvement, diffuse miliary pulmonary metastases, and osseous metastases. Disease was stage IV at post-therapy radioiodine imaging.
Clival chordoma.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with osseous metastatic disease.

High-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma of the left upper tract in a solitary kidney. Personal history also included colorectal cancer diagnosed at age 54 and metastatic prostate cancer treated with hormonal therapy with good PSA response.
Recurrent laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma following prior treatment for glottic squamous cell carcinoma.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid with central and lateral cervical nodal metastases.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma of the thyroid with metastatic disease to the lungs.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma with cervical nodal metastases.
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphocyte-depleted subtype, stage IIIB.
HPV-mediated squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil with ipsilateral cervical nodal metastasis.
Multiple myeloma, Revised International Staging System (R-ISS) stage I at diagnosis.
Bilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma, initially identified on fine-needle aspiration as papillary thyroid carcinoma.

Multiple myeloma, Revised International Staging System (R-ISS) stage II at initial diagnosis. Subsequently developed triple-class refractory relapsed/refractory disease after exposure to immunomodulatory therapy, proteasome inhibitors, and anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody therapy.
Stage IV lung cancer.
Well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue with locally advanced head and neck disease.
Poorly differentiated follicular thyroid carcinoma with locally advanced invasive disease involving the trachea and esophagus. Right vocal cord paralysis was present.

Prostate adenocarcinoma, unfavorable intermediate-risk at initial diagnosis (PSA 10.5 ng/mL, Gleason score 4+3=7 / Grade Group 3). Subsequent biochemical recurrence/progression after proton radiotherapy and short-course androgen deprivation therapy, with imaging findings suspicious for nodal metastatic disease involving pelvic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes.

Invasive lobular carcinoma of the left breast, hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, initially localized at presentation. Subsequent metastatic recurrence occurred 16 years after the primary diagnosis, involving ovary, bone, and later liver.
Neurofibromatosis type 2 with multiple intracranial and spinal extra-axial enhancing lesions consistent with meningiomatosis, bilateral vestibulocochlear schwannomas, and spinal ependymomas.
Locally advanced gastric carcinoma, diagnosed in April 2018.
Metastatic well-differentiated small bowel neuroendocrine tumor (functional/carcinoid syndrome), grade 2, with hepatic metastases and ileocolic nodal involvement at presentation.
Left temporal/insular glioma, molecularly classified as IDH-mutant lower-grade astrocytoma, molecular grade 2.

Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the right ventral oral tongue/floor of mouth. Initial clinical stage was cT1N0M0, stage I. Final pathologic stage after identification of nodal metastasis was pT1N2aM0, stage IVA.
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma of the distal ureter, clinical stage cT2N1. Nodal disease involved an upper retroperitoneal lymph node; no pelvic lymphadenopathy was identified on staging.

Poorly differentiated oncocytic thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe with extensive vascular invasion; metastatic disease to lung identified on FDG PET and confirmed by resection of a small lung lesion showing poorly differentiated oncocytic thyroid carcinoma.

Metastatic breast carcinoma, initially diagnosed in September 2013. Recurrent disease was documented in 2015 and again in April 2017, with left axillary nodal involvement and lung and liver metastases. Current symptomatic anterior chest wall/sternal mass was present by February 2018.
Right thyroid nodule with indeterminate cytology; final surgical pathology demonstrated Hurthle cell adenoma and incidental papillary thyroid microcarcinoma.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with extensive osseous metastases in the spine. Performance status was ECOG/PS 3.

High-grade squamous cell carcinoma involving the right parotid region, favored to represent metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma to an intraparotid lymph node rather than a primary salivary/parotid carcinoma.

Cutaneous melanoma of the vertex scalp, initially diagnosed in 2012. Initial stage was pT4b N2c M0, stage IIIC melanoma. Disease course included regional nodal micrometastatic involvement and in-transit metastasis in 2012, followed by recurrent regional melanoma in the right posterolateral neck in 2023 without distant metastatic disease identified.

Recurrent prostate adenocarcinoma after prior focal therapy. Initial disease had been a focal left transition zone anterior lesion, Grade Group 2. On subsequent biopsy approximately 4 years after ablation, recurrent Gleason score 4+3 adenocarcinoma was identified in the prior target lesion and in the left posterior base.
Left lower lobe lung squamous cell carcinoma, clinical stage T2N0M0.

Thyroid carcinoma of papillary type, described histologically as solid subtype papillary thyroid carcinoma. Initial thyroid FNA cytology was Bethesda IV (follicular lesion/follicular neoplasm). The patient subsequently underwent thyroid lobectomy followed by completion thyroidectomy.
Bladder cancer with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma harboring an FGFR3 alteration.
Primary lung carcinoma with metastatic lytic bone lesion involving the upper thigh/femoral region. Clinical-pathologic classification favored lung adenocarcinoma.
High-risk metastatic prostate cancer; hormone-sensitive status was referenced as relevant to treatment sequencing, but no confirmed castration-resistant disease was documented.
Stage I triple-negative breast cancer of the breast.
- Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). - Rectal adenocarcinoma, clinical stage III, cT3N1M0.

- Right thyroid Hurthle cell neoplasm on fine-needle aspiration, with Afirma gene expression classifier result reported as suspicious. - Status post thyroid lobectomy. - Final surgical pathology demonstrated a benign 3.5 cm Hurthle cell neoplasm without capsular or vascular invasion. - Incidental 1.3 cm follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma in the same lobe. - Pathologic stage described as T1b, presumed N0, Mx. - One sampled lymph node was negative for malignancy.

Follicular lymphoma, grade 3A, initially diagnosed in 2018 with supra- and infradiaphragmatic nodal disease and splenic involvement. In 2023, histologic transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma/large B-cell lymphoma arising from follicular lymphoma was documented. In 2025, second relapse with recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, germinal center subtype, was documented.

Right lower neck/upper thoracic mass with neural foraminal widening at approximately T1 level. Preoperative differential included nerve sheath tumor. CT-guided core biopsy was reported as a fibrous lesion/fibrous tumor consistent with fibromatosis. Intraoperative frozen section from the superior aspect of the mass was consistent with neurofibroma. Final permanent pathology was not available.
Hepatocellular carcinoma, status post liver transplantation, with subsequent metastatic recurrence involving the adrenal gland.

Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast carcinoma with liver metastasis. Primary breast cancer had been diagnosed in June 2012 as grade II, ER-positive, PR-positive, HER2-negative, stage T2N1 disease. Metastatic recurrence presented as a solitary liver lesion. Subsequent metastatic biopsy remained consistent with ER-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma.
Sinonasal moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with left orbital/periorbital involvement on imaging; no regional or distant metastatic disease on staging workup.
Cribriform-type adenoid cystic carcinoma originating in the right maxillary sinus, initially diagnosed in 2004; recurrent metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma to the lungs confirmed in 2021.
Left upper tract urothelial carcinoma involving the mid and distal ureter; high-grade disease without radiographic evidence of metastatic disease at staging.

Metastatic right breast invasive carcinoma with axillary, subpectoral, pulmonary, skeletal, hepatic, and bone marrow involvement. Hormone receptor profile showed ER weak positive (30%), PR negative, HER2 0; Ki-67 was high.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with bilateral thyroid microcarcinomas and cervical nodal metastases.

Hydatidiform mole. Histopathology dated 08 November 2019 showed high-grade disease consistent with hydatidiform mole. The case was initially recorded as stage I with score 6 before evacuation. After subsequent relapse/progression, pulmonary metastatic disease was described, consistent with stage III gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

Lung adenocarcinoma of the left lower lobe. Disease was found to be metastatic at the time of lobectomy in 2021 due to pleural and diaphragmatic implants, consistent with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer.

Prostate adenocarcinoma previously classified as Gleason score 3+3=6, Grade Group 1, managed with active surveillance and low-dose brachytherapy in 2008. Biochemical rise in PSA to 5 with PSMA PET findings consistent with intraprostatic recurrence/persistence. Additional PSMA-avid focus was identified in the left inferior pubic ramus, interpreted as a likely bone metastasis.
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the right lung with diffuse bone metastases.

Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe. Initial clinical stage was cT1b cN0 cM0, stage I. Final pathologic stage was pT2 pN1b, stage IVA. Incidental papillary thyroid carcinoma was also identified on final pathology.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the right thyroid lobe; primary hyperparathyroidism due to left upper parathyroid adenoma.

Graves disease diagnosed in 2003. Right thyroid lobe neoplasm resected in April 2023, reported as thyroid tumor of uncertain malignant potential. Post-thyroidectomy left thyroid bed hypoechoic lesion identified on surveillance ultrasound in 2024.

Medullary thyroid carcinoma with bulky thyroid primary causing severe tracheal compression; regional nodal metastasis in the right lateral neck; distant metastatic disease was suspected based on markedly elevated calcitonin and indeterminate pulmonary nodules. Germline RET M918T mutation was present, consistent with MEN2B.
Calcifying nested stromal-epithelial tumor of the liver with biopsy-proven pulmonary metastasis.
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma, pathologic stage T4N1, high grade.
Stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma, adenocarcinoma of the right lung, with bony metastases and soft tissue deposits.

Oncocytic thyroid carcinoma (encapsulated angioinvasive), initially localized to the left thyroid lobe; later progressive metastatic disease involving the lungs, with additional FDG-avid lesions in the thyroidectomy bed, left retropharyngeal lymph node, and C6-C7 region on follow-up PET imaging.
Acute appendicitis with incidental well-differentiated appendiceal carcinoid tumor (appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor) identified on appendectomy specimen.

Hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma centered in the post-cricoid region, clinically staged as cT4a cN2b cM0 at initial presentation. Disease later progressed with biopsy-confirmed pulmonary metastases.

Carcinoma of unknown primary at presentation, based on metastatic poorly differentiated carcinoma identified on left supraclavicular lymph node biopsy. Subsequent imaging demonstrated a pancreatic mass with metastatic disease involving liver, retroperitoneal lymph nodes, and left supraclavicular lymph node.

Mixed desmoplastic melanoma of the vertex scalp. Initial outside biopsy had been reported as desmoplastic melanoma, Breslow thickness 1.0 mm, Clark level IV, 7 mitoses/mm², no ulceration, staged pT1b. Repeat institutional biopsies from three separate scalp foci demonstrated melanoma with spindle cell proliferation, mixed desmoplastic type, depth of invasion 1.4 mm, no ulceration, no dermal mitotic figures. Clinical stage was documented as pT2a pN1c cM0, stage III, based on concern for satellite/in-transit dermal foci.
HPV-associated, p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of the left base of tongue/oropharynx with metastatic left cervical lymphadenopathy.
Stage IV lung carcinoma, initially diagnosed in July 2023 as metastatic lung cancer with EGFR-mutated disease.
- Left thyroid papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), classic type. - Left thyroid follicular carcinoma, minimally invasive.

Metastatic endometrial adenocarcinoma, initially misclassified on biopsy as cervical carcinoma. At presentation in 2012, metastatic disease was documented with supraclavicular nodal involvement and thoracic/abdominopelvic metastatic disease. Final surgical pathology after hysterectomy demonstrated endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, grade 3, with myometrial invasion and bilateral ovarian infiltration.
Destructive clival-centered skull base mass. Two endonasal biopsies identified a fibrous lesion without evidence of malignancy.
Prostate cancer.

Recurrent right parietal astrocytoma with malignant transformation. Initial diagnosis in 2015 was CNS WHO grade 2 astrocytoma. Following resection in November 2025, pathology showed astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 4, IDH-mutant.

Left breast carcinoma, initially staged clinically as cT3N1M0. Metastatic recurrent disease was identified in March 2025, involving bilateral lungs, liver, mediastinal/sternal nodal disease, skeleton, and brain/pituitary-sellar region.
Malignant sinonasal mucosal melanoma centered in the right maxillary sinus, initially staged as cT4a versus cT4b N0 M0.
High-grade serous carcinoma of bilateral ovaries, FIGO stage IIIA after interval cytoreduction; ypT3aN0.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the supraglottic larynx/epiglottis, clinically staged as cT1N0M0.
Cutaneous melanoma of the right lower eyelid. Initial biopsy indicated at least pT4b disease with Breslow thickness at least 4.7 mm. Final pathologic stage was pT4bN0, corresponding to stage IIC.

Skin adnexal adenocarcinoma of the left chest wall, reported as syringocystadenocarcinoma/syringocystidinocarcinoma, with subsequent axillary nodal recurrence and later metastatic recurrence involving lungs and pleura.

Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma, staged as cT4N1M0 / stage T4N1 with no distant metastases identified on PET. Lesion was located 5 cm from the anal verge. Mesorectal fascia involvement was present.

Right parieto-temporal brain tumor diagnosed on 20 March 2025. Initial diagnosis after first surgery was ependymoma. Following re-excision on 11 October 2025, the lesion from the right temporal lobe was diagnosed as desmoplastic infantile astrocytoma. Stage at diagnosis was documented as stage II. Performance status at diagnosis was 2.
Locally advanced left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, stage IIIB, with axillary lymph node involvement; estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor positive, HER2 negative.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma, infiltrative follicular subtype, involving the right thyroid with metastatic cervical lymph node disease. Residual/recurrent cervical nodal disease and suspected contralateral thyroid involvement were subsequently identified.
p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil with ipsilateral cervical nodal metastasis and ipsilateral retropharyngeal lymph node involvement; clinical stage T2N1.

Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the right nasal cavity/anterior nasal passage, with cribriform and tubular histologic patterns. Initial postoperative stage was documented as T3N0Mx. Recurrent disease later involved an anterior site and a posterior pterygopalatine fossa (PPF) region site.

Stage IIIB lung squamous cell carcinoma with mediastinal nodal involvement. ECOG performance status was 1. Comorbidities included type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. The patient was a non-smoker.
Thymoma, clinically staged as stage III on the basis of locally invasive mediastinal mass involving major neck vessels. No distant metastases were identified at initial staging.

Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma involving both thyroid lobes, with aggressive histologic variants (columnar cell and tall cell variant with hobnail features), extrathyroidal extension into strap muscles, intraoperative tracheal invasion, cervical nodal metastases, pulmonary metastasis, and liver lesion described as consistent with metastasis. Concurrent primary hyperparathyroidism due to left upper parathyroid adenoma.

Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the left floor of mouth with synchronous metastatic pulmonary disease at initial staging; later metastatic involvement included pleural-based thoracic lesions and a renal lesion.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), pre-cabazitaxel, with extensive osseous metastatic disease.
Stage IV right lung adenocarcinoma with nodal and hepatic metastatic disease at presentation. Subsequent progression included osseous metastatic disease.

Papillary thyroid carcinoma, primary tumor 1.3 cm, staged postoperatively as pT1bN1a. Disease was confined to the thyroid on preoperative imaging, with one small central compartment lymph node metastasis identified on surgical pathology.

Third ventricular mass causing obstructive hydrocephalus. Differential diagnosis discussed in the record included primary intraventricular craniopharyngioma, glial neoplasm/astrocytoma, optic pathway glioma, hypothalamic glioma, and germinoma.
Multifocal high-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder with concomitant carcinoma in situ (CIS); high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
Endometrial adenocarcinoma.
Non-small cell lung carcinoma, adenocarcinoma of the left lung. Final recorded clinical stage was T4N3M0.

Stage IV well-differentiated low-grade neuroendocrine tumor with hepatic metastases and mesenteric nodal disease, consistent with functional metastatic neuroendocrine tumor/carcinoid syndrome. Subsequent metastatic recurrence/progression included cervical soft tissue metastasis and extensive osseous metastatic disease.

Cutaneous melanoma of the posterior scalp with regional nodal metastases. Clinical stage was T2b N2b M0, stage IIIB. Disease involved the posterior scalp primary and right cervical/supraclavicular nodal basin. No distant metastatic disease was identified on staging or restaging imaging.
Left breast triple-negative invasive carcinoma, clinical stage cT2N1M0, stage IIB at initial diagnosis. Subsequent metastatic recurrence involving lung, bone, and metastatic lymph nodes.
Low-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma involving the renal pelvis/calyceal system. Subsequent non-muscle-invasive bladder tumor recurrence was identified.
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), 3 cm lesion in hepatic segments 2-3, with adjacent segmental portal vein tumor invasion; described as BCLC stage C.
Carcinoma ovary, diagnosed in 2019. Disease was described as platinum-resistant after progression on gemcitabine/carboplatin.
High-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the left nasal sidewall/face; synchronous basal cell carcinoma of the left lower eyelid; carcinoma in situ of the left forehead.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the sinonasal region involving the left ethmoid/nasal cavity with orbital invasion and skull base involvement.

Multifocal differentiated thyroid carcinoma following surgery, consisting of: - Right follicular thyroid carcinoma, minimally invasive type - Left papillary thyroid carcinoma, classical type - Additional incidental papillary thyroid microcarcinoma - Central neck lymph node metastases (3 involved lymph nodes, all small-volume) Overall stage was documented as stage I low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma of the left thyroid lobe.
Abdominal neuroblastoma, staged as L2 disease after evaluation. Primary mass was located in the left upper quadrant/upper abdomen.
Multifocal high-grade glioma, with histopathologic features favoring astrocytoma, WHO grade 4.
Posterior pharyngeal wall hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

Left breast invasive hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, status post breast-conserving surgery, with 1 of 2 sentinel lymph nodes positive. Systemic staging showed no evidence of distant metastatic disease.

Prostate adenocarcinoma previously treated with robotic radical prostatectomy in 2020. Post-prostatectomy biochemical persistence/recurrence was present, with PSA never becoming undetectable. Subsequent evaluation identified a large bladder neck/prostate bed mass on multiparametric MRI; biopsies of this tissue showed benign prostatic hyperplasia and inflammation without carcinoma. PSMA PET demonstrated focal uptake in the prostate bed, a right iliac bone lesion, and low-level rib uptake. Axumin PET demonstrated focal uptake in the prostate bed mass without corresponding uptake in the right ilium or ribs.
Carcinoma base of tongue, clinical stage cT2N1.
